deep.reconstruction:
This page holds no derivation. It is three lines of pencil notes in German, in the natural-philosophy bundle, beginning at the top of an otherwise blank sheet. The notes break off in mid-sentence. They concern the physical meaning of a potential function and a density in Riemann's speculative theory of aether or space and matter. They have nothing to do with the theta-function and Abelian-integral computations on the next folio (146), which belong to another context.

Line-by-line reading:

(1) A potential 𝔙 is considered at a point (x,y,z) and at the neighbouring point (x+dx,y,z). This is presumably groundwork for a difference quotient ∂𝔙/∂x, i.e. a force component -∂𝔙/∂x; that reading is my inference, as no formula is written. Then: 'and material atom', with 'durch' inserted above. ϱ is the density (Dichtigkeit). 𝔙 is the 'Potential der ...kraft'; the last word is unclear, either 'Schwerkraft' (gravity) or an aether force.

(2) The density ϱ is read as the 'Grad der Verbindung', the degree of union or binding. 'The striving of the space-atom toward union is represented ...' The words 'zu Verbindung' are struck through and replaced by 'des Raumatoms auf'. Then 'Wofern V ...' begins.

(3) '... the striving of the space-atom (Raumatom) toward union with this material atom, V the ...', where the text breaks off.

The idea being drafted is a physical interpretation of the two quantities of potential theory. The density ϱ measures how far elements of space or aether are bound to ponderable matter. The potential V measures the tendency (Streben) of a space element to unite with a material atom. The force on such an element would then follow from the variation of V between neighbouring points.

This fits the programme of Riemann's posthumously published 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' and related fragments (Werke, 1876/1892). There, gravitation and light are explained by a space-filling substance whose interaction with ponderable atoms is described through potential functions. The governing relation would be Poisson's equation ΔV = -4πϱ, but it does not appear on the page; I supply it as context only.

No computation is performed, so there is nothing to verify step by step.

results.what: Interpretation of mass density ϱ as the 'degree of union' of space(-atoms) with matter, and of the potential V as the 'striving' of a space-atom to unite with a material atom; set up with neighbouring points (x,y,z), (x+dx,y,z) for a gradient
